decision.question: Post about building an AI agent team that runs your companies?
decision.recommendation: This is your strongest angle right now. You literally have AI agents doing VC research, writing outreach, building content — while you sleep. The 'night shift' concept is gold. Rephrase in your voice, keep it raw.
evidence: Night shift log shows 3 sub-agents delivered VC lists, investor emails, and webinar content in one session
Agent team concept is unique — most founders talk about using ChatGPT, you have an actual AI COO
'Building in public' content about AI agents gets massive engagement right now

options.label: Post as text
options.description:
DRAFT (rephrase this):

Hook: Last night I went to sleep and woke up to 3 deliverables I didn't make.

Body: I've been building something weird. Instead of hiring a team, I built one. AI agents that actually do the work — not chatbots, not copilots. Agents.

Last night while I slept, my system:
- Researched 20 venture capital firms in Benelux for one of my companies
- Wrote a full investor outreach email sequence
- Built LinkedIn DM templates for 4 different customer personas

I'm 20. I don't have a team of 15. I have a system that works at 3AM.

This is what I mean when I say AI isn't about replacing people — it's about what becomes possible when a solo founder can operate like a company.

Building OttoGen to help other businesses do exactly this.

Key points: night shift concept, solo founder with AI team, actual deliverables not theory, OttoGen mention at end

options.label: Record video
options.description: 30-45 sec, phone camera, casual. Say something like: 'So I woke up this morning and had 3 finished deliverables sitting in my system. VC research, outreach emails, LinkedIn templates. I didn't make any of them. My AI agents did it while I was asleep. I'm 20, running multiple companies, and I basically have a team that works 24/7 for free. This is what building with AI actually looks like — not asking ChatGPT to write your emails. I'm talking actual autonomous agents doing real work. Wild times.'
